messages:
jess: Quick heads-up — found a weird perf regression on the paged+interleaved KV path when running flash_hybrid on Hopper. p50 jumped from ~12ms to ~34ms and throughput dropped ~55% for long-context chat workload.
omar: ack. did this surface after the dtype/packing change last week?
jess: probably. we changed the default dtype packing for bf16 -> packed-bf16 (2-byte packed) in the last runtime patch. I have a short perf log below.
liam: can you paste the harness command + outputs?
jess: sure. command we ran: ```./perf/harness --model=redwood/opt-12b --kernel=flash_hybrid --kv-layout=interleaved --dtype=bf16 --seq=4096 --batch=2 --prefill=512```
jess: baseline (old binary, separate-layout): p50=11.8ms, tokens/s=920
jess: after change (new binary, interleaved): p50=34.1ms, tokens/s=410
perf-bot: [auto-report] attached flamegraph -> /perf/artifacts/2034567890/flame.svg :eyes:
omar: flame shows hot-spots in the KV gather kernel and large stalls in shared memory loads (bank conflicts).
liam: interesting — interleaved layout introduces non-linear strides across banks if stride*elem_size % 128 != 0, right?
sara: yep. on Hopper the L2+shared behavior is more sensitive to 128B coalescing. If packing changed element_size from 2 to assumed 4 somewhere, stride math could be wrong and cause bank straddles.
jess: i instrumented the stride and alignment: for seq=4096, kv_entries=4608, element_bytes=2, per-row stride computed = 4608*2 = 9216 bytes -> 9216 % 128 == 0, so seems aligned. but the issue shows up only with interleaved layout and bf16.
liam: could there be a kernel code path that promotes bf16 to 32-bit regs and writes back 4-byte stores (temporarily) causing misalignment? eg a pack/unpack bug in fused-copy that uses `float` store for lane temp.
omar: also check the vectorized store path: `st.global.v4.u32` vs `st.global.u16`. If a conditional chooses the wrong store width under certain flags, writes will misalign subsequent rows.
jess: added quick checks: memory dump from device shows occasional 4-byte tiles in the interleaved region. so likely a stray 32-bit store.
sara: that would explain bank conflicts and L2 write-combine churn. Repro plan: 1) rerun with `--kv-layout=separate` 2) rerun with `--dtype=float16` 3) inject conservative alignment padding to make stride multiple of 256 4) run nvprof/NSight to capture store instructions.
jess: did 1 & 3 already: separate layout restores perf (p50=12.2ms), padding to 256-byte stride also restores perf (p50=13.0ms). float16 run: partial improvement (p50=20ms) but not fully fixed.
liam: nice triage. that rules in mis-sized store. can you dump disassembly of the memcpy/fused-copy kernel for bf16 path? look for `st.global.v4.f32` or similar.
jess: grabbing it now, will attach. snippet: ```// fused_copy_bf16.sass
// ...
st.global.b64 [rA], rB; // expected 2xbf16 per 4-byte store
// but we see code path using st.global.u32 for some lanes
```
perf-bot: regression ticket created: INF-2147 (linked to this thread).
sara: mitigation: add a temporary kernel-selection override in the selector so interleaved+bf16 chooses separate-layout or the safe memcpy path until patch lands. small config: ```{
  "overrides": [
    { "kernel": "flash_hybrid", "dtype": "bf16", "kv_layout": "interleaved", "action": "prefer", "fallback": "separate" }
  ]
}```
omar: also add a nightly test that runs long-context chat (seq=4096) on Hopper images with both layouts to catch regressions.
liam: I'll send a quick CL that forces explicit `st.global.u16` on the bf16 store path and run microbench.
jess: thanks — assigned INF-2147 to liam. immediate action: push kernel-select override to canary hosts, add a perf-monitor alert for p50>25ms on chat-long route.
sara: +1. add note to release notes and rollback plan.
jess: summary: cause = stray 32-bit store in bf16 interleaved fused-copy -> bank conflicts and L2 churn; workaround = selector override -> separate layout/padding; fix in flight = kernel codepath patch to use 16-bit stores.
omar: awesome triage. keep updates here as you have them. :thumbsup:
